findings.ref: MCC-08 (finite timeouts, batch limits), GR-16 cost, README claim 'после аудита меняется только backend.py'
findings.problem: The port is synchronous and has no limit. Case 1: a real KB adapter doing blocking HTTP inside Backend.search runs inside an async handler. asyncio.wait_for cannot interrupt it, so manifest timeout_s never fires, and a hung KB blocks every call of the process. Case 2: a query matching 10,000 documents fetches all full texts on every page, because documents_search recomputes the full list and slices it. The real KB can't be plugged in without changing the port and the tools, which goes against the scaffold's own claim.
findings.required_improvement: Make the KB port async (or run it in a thread with a cancellable client timeout). Pass limit/cursor to the backend, not slice after it. Keep the per-item check. Add tests: a slow async backend times out to temporarily_unavailable; search asks the backend for at most limit+1 items.

findings.problem: M5.json is regenerated from runs that include the M6 tests (35 instead of 29), so a kb failure turns the closed M5 report red. '|| true' after the M6 report hides an M6-only failure. CI uploads only M5.json, so M6 evidence never reaches CI artifacts.
findings.required_improvement: Upload M6.json in the m5-stand job. Drop '|| true'. Do not commit a regenerated M5.json from M6 cycles, or record in M6.json that M5.json was regenerated.

findings.problem: Test time rose from about 336 s to about 445 s per run (executor's M6.json, confirmed by my fresh run: 458 s). Three runs are about 22-23 min of tests, plus two image builds, three compose ups and a bootstrap. STAND_WALL. A cold GitHub runner is close to the 30-minute kill.
findings.required_improvement: Raise the timeout (e.g. 45) or make the kb stand tests cheaper (one docker compose logs read per test instead of per assertion).

scaffold_assessment.summary: The access-independent part is careful and mostly right. The isolation logic (identity -> schema -> bundle -> grants -> KB, GR-16/17, SC-05 identical not_found, zero KB calls on refusal) is correct, well tested (40 unit, 6 stand tests, mutmut-clean in tools/backend) and reruns green through ContextForge. The reports are honest about what is blocked. It will not close without rework after access, though. The claim 'after the audit only backend.py changes' does not hold: the port must become async and bounded (F5), and the tools must bound KB data to their schemas (F2).
